archetypes.name: wire-contract
archetypes.rationale: Checks that the issue-anchor and scope-reduction marker contract is consistently wired across scout, reviewer, voter, tally, aggregation, docs, and tests.
archetypes.prompt_body: Trace the proposed scope-anchor and [SCOPE-REDUCTION] contracts end to end against the listed files. Look for wrong source selection between original issue, brainstorm-merged context, current plan, and baseline plan, plus flag-name or semantic drift between shell scripts, docs, and harnesses. Pay special attention to stages that silently degrade or reuse shared scripts because a partial contract can make reviewers or voters re-enter plan-bloat mode. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: fallback-artifacts
archetypes.rationale: Targets plan defects in fallback and artifact paths where protected scope-cut acceptance could be lost or misclassified despite correct normal voting.
archetypes.prompt_body: Examine the proposed MainAgent 0-judge path, tally override, accepted-findings artifacts, and findings-classification TSV behavior as one correctness chain. Hunt for cases where a tagged scope-reduction finding wins conceptually but is later forced back to rejected, omitted from accepted artifacts, or mishandled when exonerated. Also check whether dedup and aggregation fallback behavior preserves enough evidence for tally without broadening the marker detector. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: compatibility-harness
archetypes.rationale: Reviews whether the plan’s shared-script compatibility promises and regression coverage are specific enough to prevent unintended prompt or voter changes outside design review.
archetypes.prompt_body: Validate the plan’s no-flag byte-identical promises for shared prompt and voter scripts against the proposed test updates. Look for missing harness assertions around omitted flags, unchanged non-design consumers, Makefile registration, and negative cases for non-leading or code-fenced scope markers. Treat vague test bullets as defects when they do not pin down the compatibility contract the implementation must preserve. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
